headline: shadcn/improve
abstract: Use your most capable model to audit your codebase and write plans for cheaper models to execute.improve An agent skill that audits any codebase and writes implementation plans for other agents to execute. The idea: use your most capable model for the part where intelligence compounds — understanding the codebase, judging what's worth doing, writing the spec — and hand execution to cheaper models. The skill never implements anything itself. The plan is the product. you → /improve (expensive model, advises) plans/ → 001-fix-n-plus-one.md (self-contained specs) other agent → implements, tests, ships (cheap model, executes) Install npx skills add shadcn/improve Works in any agent that supports Agent Skills format. headline: So so true 🇺🇸

Why are old stories that were not even covered up all that well become sudden international and geopolitical news? The timing is suspicious, so worth asking: who benefits and why now? If Jensen, the premier champion of open models, is taken out then anyone who wants AI closed, centralized, and controlled might benefit. Why now? The midterms seem relevant. But also perhaps the upcoming IPOs.

I scraped 803 companies sub-processors to investigate what AI native companies are using for their infrastructure.. Some interesting findings from the last time I did this in March: > 44% of companies list two+ model providers (up from 33%). Small n, but Anthropic grew twice as fast as OpenAI. > 86 pairs where each company names the other as a subprocessor (@AnthropicAI + @Cloudflare, @vercel + @SpaceXSI) > 33% of companies list an inference provider (up from 22%). @modal continues to crush. > Chinese models are primarily coming through video (think Bytedance) rather than text (at least on the subprocessor lists) > @typesafeai is the breakout hit, going from 0 to many companies in a short period. Caveat: subprocessor lists tend to be a lagging indicator, but a sure shot way of knowing if the company is using something. You can find all the updated data, design and insights at deploygraph dot com. Feedback welcome!
